entries.name: Grey red-backed vole
behaviour: builds surface runways to burrows
freezes, then bolts in zigzag dashes when uncovered
population booms and crashes on ~3-4 year cycles
entries.notes: A grey-mantled cousin of the ruddy bank vole; its cyclic outbreaks feed the hawk owls and weasels. Tiny voxel footprint, ideal swarm ambient.

entries.name: Short-tailed field vole
behaviour: sub-surface nest chambers with grass linings
close-cropped lawn patches reveal runways
grazing on fresh growth under snow
entries.notes: Grassland-taiga edge specialist; fields near the taiga turn ankle-high runs in summer. The vole most likely to be unlucky under an adder's coil.

entries.name: Common shrew
behaviour: must eat most of its body weight each day or starve within hours
red-tipped iron-pigmented teeth
uses ultrasonic twittering to sense surroundings in the dark
entries.notes: The restless grey spark under the leaf litter; almost impossible to keep alive in captivity. Good ambient detail: fast, hyperactive, inoffensive to watch.

entries.name: Eurasian water shrew
behaviour: dives after underwater prey with a silvery countershaded back
fur holds an air bubble, glowing silver underwater
trots along stream margins with a two-footed gallop
entries.notes: The only shrew that hunts underwater; its silver belly shines when it surfaces near a taiga brook. A quiet sign of unpolluted water.

entries.name: Eurasian water vole
behaviour: burrows into steep banks with gnawed 'lawns' above water
plops into water at the first shadow, swimming underwater to safety
winters on stored roots and bark caches underwater
entries.notes: Europe's fastest-collapsing rodent; American mink arrivals wiped out whole bank populations. A test subject for rivers recovering from eutrophication.

entries.name: Siberian chipmunk
behaviour: stuffs cheek pouches and lopes home with a full cheek bulge
hibernates in log-stack burrows, waking every few days to snack
streaked-backed; dashes with tail erect when alarmed
entries.notes: The striped squirrel of the larch taiga; bold and charismatic, now spreading as an invasive across western Europe. Ideal for a friendly forest encounter.

entries.name: Northern birch mouse
behaviour: prehensile tail for gripping twigs and canes
hibernates October to May, tail wrapped around itself like a crockery handle
single black spine stripe runs from muzzle to rump
entries.notes: A jumping mouse in taiga disguise — your players will mistake it for a mouse with a tail depending on the light. Hibernation makes it a winter easter egg.

entries.name: Daurian hedgehog
behaviour: gravel digging at dusk for beetle larvae
curls into a full spine ball when cornered
hibernates from November in loose-soil dens
entries.notes: The carp-like spine capsule of the eastern taiga margin. Slower and longer-snouted than the European hedgehog, and rarer in game form.

entries.name: American mink

breeding.season: late winter mating; implantation delayed until spring

behaviour: fishes the shallows with a stiff-tailed dive
dens in bank hollows with bedding of down
introduced in Eurasia, where it has savaged native water vole and European mink
entries.notes: North America's riverbank assassin; on Eurasian rivers it is an ecological horror. Gestation_days is null because of the long implantation delay.

entries.name: Siberian weasel
behaviour: arboreal and terrestrial; jaunts the canopy like a tube
caches prey in tree forks
the Japanese subspecies (itatsi) was introduced as a ratter and is now common
entries.notes: The sable's little brother: brighter orange, thinner tail, no taste for salmon. Bandit mask and tail-tip distinguish it from the ermine.

entries.name: American marten

breeding.season: midsummer mating; implantation delayed until spring

behaviour: lives almost entirely in old-growth conifer forest
dens under root wads, in snags and log piles
soft, glossy fur coveted by fur trade; recovery fuels old-growth debates
entries.notes: The New World sable; an interior-forest indicator species. Gestation_days is null because of the ~9-month delayed implantation.

entries.name: European polecat
behaviour: stinks like a skunk when provoked; a defensive musk gland
long, low loping hunt along hedges and dykes
ancestor of the ferret — polecat means 'piglet of the woods'
entries.player: huntable; tamable: yes (ferrets derive from it)
entries.notes: The skunk-fumes of the taiga margin — and the wild source of every ferret. Open woodland and river valleys, not dense spruce.

entries.name: Daubenton's bat
entries.migrates: short local movements between summer roosts and winter hibernacula

breeding.season: summer; maternity colonies roost in cavities

behaviour: skims water surface harpooning emerging midges with feet
maternity colonies in bridges, culverts and tree hollows
hibernates deep in caves and mines below frost
entries.notes: The water-trawling bat; feeding over taiga brooks on still evenings is its whole identity. A health indicator for headwater streams.

entries.name: Northern bat
entries.migrates: mostly resident; some southern populations non-migratory

breeding.season: summer; colonies in buildings and rock crevices

behaviour: the northernmost-breeding bat on Earth
roosts in alpine rock crevices above the treeline
one of the few bats that tolerates genuinely cold summers
entries.notes: A bat at 69 north; it resolves every 'nothing can live here' joke about the taiga. Winter hibernacula in alpine talus.

entries.name: Common crossbill
entries.migrates: nomadic irruptions following cone crops; southern invasions when mast fails

breeding.season: any month with ripe cones; often midwinter

behaviour: crossed mandibles pry scales apart; sideways lever, not a beak
breeds in January if cones allow — song can pierce a blizzard
calls a ringing 'jip-jip' from larch crowns high overhead
entries.notes: The finch with scissors for a bill; its irruptive years will make the whole taiga ring. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Pine grosbeak
entries.migrates: nomadic; irrupts south after cone failures
behaviour: herds of chunky rose-breasted finches strip rowan in autumn
clambers treetops like a parrot rather than fluttering
slow, mournful 'tew-tew' note carries through foggy larch woods
entries.notes: The taiga's biggest, gentlest finch; a rosy blur that wanders with the cone crop. Winter flocks glow in hoarfrost mornings.

entries.name: Bohemian waxwing
entries.migrates: nomadic winter irruptions; flocks wander hundreds of kilometres
behaviour: crested, silky and masked; wing tips carry sealing-wax-red tips
flocks stripped rowans in a holographic blur at dusk
feeds on fermented berries and can become tipsy

voxel_model.pattern: butter-yellow tail tip, red wing wax

entries.notes: The silkiest bird in the northern woods; a winter irruption can fill every rowan for a week then vanish entirely.

entries.name: Brambling
entries.migrates: strong winter irruptions far south when mast fails; roosts of millions recorded
behaviour: breeds in birch-spruce taiga, winters in beech mast woods
roosting flocks can number in the millions — the taiga's standing pulse
male flashes a burning orange shoulder in flight
entries.notes: One birch-mast year can drop a flock of a million onto one field; the sound is like rain on a tin roof. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Common redpoll
entries.migrates: irruptive southward in winter when birch crops fail
behaviour: hitches upside-down along birch twigs stripping seeds from catkins
flocks undulate like loose confetti over stubble
streaky 'red-poll' song ends each stanza with a buzzy trill
entries.notes: Often rests in weed piles and track verges; a fading red forehead is the field mark from a moving sled. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Boreal chickadee
behaviour: fluffs to a sphere against deep cold; food caches raided in seconds
call is a hoarse 'chick-a-day-dee-dee' scold
soft rusty flanks separate it from the black-capped cousin

voxel_model.pattern: dark cap, brown back, rusty flanks

entries.notes: The North American taiga's grey-capped titmouse; needs whole swampy spruce forests to persist. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Coal tit
entries.migrates: partial migrant; some populations move south in winter
behaviour: spends its whole life in conifer needles; acrobatic upside-down feeder
nests in forest-floor nooks, stone walls and upturned roots
white nape patch flashes like a signal lamp at distance
entries.notes: The smallest European titmouse and the taiga's purest conifer specialist; clutches of 9-11 eggs power the canopy food web.

entries.name: Black-backed woodpecker
entries.migrates: irrupts to burned forests after spruce beetle outbreaks
behaviour: specialist of burned and bug-killed spruce forests
pecks bark scales flat off snags to strip beetle tunnels
flies with a bounding, roller-coaster flight between trees

voxel_model.pattern: solid black back, white cheek bar, red crown on males

entries.notes: The fire-chaser of the North American taiga; where spruce beetles kill a stand, this woodpecker follows like a clockwork strike.

entries.name: Hazel grouse
behaviour: sticks to dense understorey and never perches high
male drums burst of wing-whirring at dusk in the spruce
bobwhite-like whistle announces it long before sight

voxel_model.pattern: ruff below beak, barred flanks, black throat bib

entries.notes: The forest hen of the European taiga edge; a whispery grouse modeled as a darting russet blur between trunks. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Great grey shrike
entries.migrates: residents sedentary; northern breeders drift south in winter
behaviour: watches from isolated snags and telegraph posts, impaling prey on thorns
aerial butcher-bird gymnastics: grapples voles mid-air
grey-and-white, silent but never still — motion stops only to strike

voxel_model.pattern: black mask and wings, white wing bar

entries.notes: The Butcher-bird of the open taiga; a laden cache of impaled voles on a dead pine is its hunting signature for days.

entries.name: Northern hawk owl
entries.migrates: irruptive after vole crashes; wanders far south of the taiga in winter
behaviour: hunts in broad daylight, sitting bolt upright on an isolated snag
plunges to the ground feet-first after voles under grass
nests in old woodpecker holes, never in open nests
entries.notes: The owl that refuses the night; its bright orange eyes on pale cheeks stare from spruce tops over bogs. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Eurasian pygmy owl
behaviour: Europe's smallest owl; fits in a two-handed teacup
hunts songbirds at dusk with a shrike-like perch-and-pounce
grey-streaked back studded with white crown spots
entries.notes: A wren-sized broadcaster for hours at dusk; loop its whistle and every coal tit in earshot will scold back. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Arctic grayling
entries.migrates: short upstream spawning runs in spring; overwinters in deep pools
behaviour: sail-like dorsal fin streaked with crimson and cobalt spots
flashes and angers under willow root shade
one of the few salmonids that is mostly hand-raised by sight, not scent

voxel_model.pattern: purple-and-rust dorsal sail with red streaks

entries.notes: The taiga river's most elegant fish; fly-fishers crossing the Arctic circle chase exactly this species. Cold, clean, oxygen-rich water obligatory.

entries.name: Lenok
behaviour: sharp-snouted and blunt-snouted forms, both deep-bellied trouts
the largest salmonid after the taimen; a trophy in Siberian rivers
dark brown spots over bronze flanks; reddish pectoral fins
entries.notes: Siberia's mountain trout; rare in the south of its range, abundant higher up. Blunt-snouted kin handles both the Amur and the Yangtze.

entries.name: Burbot
entries.migrates: winter spawning migrations under ice, January to March
behaviour: the only freshwater cod; a single barbel on the chin
spawns beneath the ice at night, a sociable throng
oily liver is a northern delicacy, sold in jars
entries.notes: The taiga's own ling; it will take a night-time baited hook as readily as a swimming minnow. The liver is famous; the rest is work.

entries.name: White-spotted char
entries.migrates: anadromous populations run upriver to spawn in autumn
behaviour: white-spotted flanks; olive back, rusty sides
found in cold fast headwaters and lake outlets
rasbora-like flash when it turns in runs
entries.notes: The classic headwater char of the Amur and Sakhalin; resident now in Japanese mountains under the same name (iwana).

entries.name: Siberian salamander
entries.migrates: spring migration to breeding pools in thaw weeks

breeding.season: may and early june; up to 240 eggs in gelatinous sacs

behaviour: survives freezing to -50 C: expels a quarter of its body water as ice and floods its cells with glycerol
thaws out of permafrost alive when the thaw reaches it
bluish-brown with a violet dorsal stripe; tail longer than body
entries.notes: The coldest-surviving vertebrate on Earth; body fluids freeze solid yet it revives in spring. A taiga immortality cameo, not a food item.

entries.name: Viviparous lizard

breeding.season: summer; female gives live birth in August and September

behaviour: the northernmost reptile on Earth
basks crouched on warm stones, puffed sides flat to the sun
some southern populations lay eggs; cold north shores live-bearing only

voxel_model.pattern: spotted and streaked flanks; male with orange belly

entries.notes: A reptile at a latitude where most lizards cannot exist, because it skips the egg stage. Basks wherever the sun bleeds through canopy gaps.

entries.name: Common adder

breeding.season: spring mating; ovoviviparous birth in August and September

behaviour: zigzag dorsal chevron; black herringbone in melanistic males
communal hibernacula in stony sunny banks, dozens per den
venom rarely dangerous to adults; keep encounters honest, not slasher-film
entries.notes: Northern Europe's only venomous snake; the zigzag is the one thing every northern hiker learns to scan for. Melanism common in the cold.

entries.name: Common toad
entries.migrates: spring migration to natal ponds, sometimes for km

breeding.season: april and may; spawn in double strings

behaviour: warted skin with toxic parotoid glands behind the eyes
plods across meadows at dusk eating slugs en route
explosive breeder: a single warm night can fill a pond with spawn
entries.notes: The warty garden toad of the taiga margin; harmless if left alone. Spawn strings look like dark rice noodles wound on twigs.

entries.name: European spruce bark beetle
entries.migrates: mass flights disperse to stressed spruce after storms and heatwaves

breeding.season: spring and high summer; two generations per year

behaviour: the most destructive forest insect in Europe; fells million-hectare spruce stands
males excavate nuptial chamber, attract females with aggregation pheromone
galleries fan out under the bark in a double-forked pattern
sounds: faint rustling under bark in outbreak years
entries.notes: A 5 mm insect that out-competes spruce in drought years; whole stands die in two summers. The reason so much Central European taiga is brown.

entries.name: Common hawker

breeding.season: july to september; three-year aquatic larvae

behaviour: patrols bog pools hawking midges in still afternoons
larvae stalk tadpoles and caddisflies underwater for years
males blue-and-green mosaic, females brown with green

voxel_model.pattern: blue mosaic under windows with green stripes

entries.notes: The bog hawker; the taiga's only common large dragonfly of cold blanket bog. Their larval lifespan outlasts the observer, not the observer's patience.

entries.name: Freshwater pearl mussel

breeding.season: summer; larvae (glochidia) ride gills of trout and grayling for months

behaviour: centuries-old filter clams lined along clean oxygenated gravel beds
produces the operculated rosy pearl; overharvest drove it near extinction
larvae need living salmonid hosts to metamorphose

voxel_model.pattern: dark spotted periostracum, nacred rosy interior

entries.notes: A sessile taiga witness — some beds are older than the forest around them. Sensitive to silt and acidification; a canary for headwaters.
